message.content: {"passages":[{"reference":"1.9","text":"When I said, “I would like to meet one of those who had seen him,” they immediately led me away, saying, “There is someone here who has not only met him personally but also comes from the land over there—a Hebrew man named Barnabas. He says that he himself is one of his disciples, and while sitting somewhere around here, he readily tells anyone who wishes the words of his promise.” So I went with them. When I arrived, I stood with the crowd that was present and listened to his words. I perceived that he was speaking the truth, not with dialectical technique, but guilelessly and without preparation, setting out the things he had heard and had seen the Son of God who appeared do and say. He also furnished many witnesses to the wonders and sayings he recounted, including many from the very crowd that was present.","lexical_decisions":[{"source_quote":"ἱστορήσας αὐτὸν","chosen":"met him personally","rationale":"With a person as its object, ἱστορέω can denote visiting or becoming personally acquainted with someone, not merely learning information about him."},{"source_quote":"τῆς ἐκεῖθεν γῆς ὑπάρχων","chosen":"comes from the land over there","rationale":"Preserves the source’s deictic and geographically nonspecific description of Barnabas’s origin."},{"source_quote":"τῆς ἐκείνου ὑποσχέσεως τοὺς λόγους","chosen":"the words of his promise","rationale":"Retains the promise terminology and the pronoun’s reference without replacing it with a more familiar theological expression."},{"source_quote":"ἅ τε ἤκουσεν καὶ ἑόρακεν τὸν τοῦ θεοῦ φανέντα υἱὸν πεποιηκέναι τε καὶ εἰρηκέναι","chosen":"the things he had heard and had seen the Son of God who appeared do and say","rationale":"Preserves both hearing and seeing, the Son’s appearance, and the paired actions of doing and speaking."},{"source_quote":"καὶ ἐξ αὐτοῦ τοῦ παρεστῶτος ὄχλου","chosen":"including many from the very crowd that was present","rationale":"The witnesses supplied by Barnabas included people drawn from the crowd then present."}],"source_issues":[]},{"reference":"1.10","text":"Because the crowds were favorably disposed toward what was being said without cunning, the philosophers whose starting point was worldly education began to laugh at him and mock him, jeering and deriding him with boundless audacity, as though they were wielding syllogisms as mighty weapons. But he, repelling their nonsense, would not join in their crafty questioning. Remaining undaunted, he did not stop speaking. Once someone asked him why a gnat had come into being and, though extremely small and having six feet, also has wings, while an elephant, the largest of animals, has only four feet and no wings. After the question, he took up the discourse that had been interrupted and, as though he had answered the question, resumed the discourse set before him from the beginning, using only this preface after each interruption: “We have been commanded only to tell you the words and wonderful deeds of the one who sent us, and instead of a logical demonstration we present to you many witnesses from among those of you who are here. I remember their faces as living images, sufficient testimonies. What remains is in your power: to yield or to disobey. But I will not cease telling you what benefits you, because for me silence is loss, while for you disobedience is harm. I could also provide demonstrations in answer to your speculative questions, if you were asking in a truth-loving spirit. But now is not a suitable time to tell you the reason for the differing creation of the gnat and the elephant, since you are ignorant of the God of the universe.”","lexical_decisions":[{"source_quote":"ἐκ παιδείας κοσμικῆς ὁρμώμενοι","chosen":"whose starting point was worldly education","rationale":"The participle identifies worldly education as the basis from which the philosophers proceeded."},{"source_quote":"οὐ συνέτρεχεν αὐτῶν τῇ πανούργῳ πεύσει","chosen":"would not join in their crafty questioning","rationale":"The wording depicts his refusal to run along with or participate in their line of questioning, not an inability to answer."},{"source_quote":"ὡς πρὸς τὴν πεῦσιν ἀποκρινάμενος","chosen":"as though he had answered the question","rationale":"ὡς presents his resumption of the main discourse as functioning like an answer, although he does not explain the animals directly."},{"source_quote":"ὧν ἐγὼ τὰ εἴδη μέμνημαι ὡς ἐμψύχους εἰκόνας ἱκανὰς μαρτυρίας","chosen":"I remember their faces as living images, sufficient testimonies","rationale":"εἴδη may denote the witnesses’ visible forms or faces; “faces” suits the claim that Barnabas remembers the people serving as living testimony."},{"source_quote":"τῶν εἰκαίων ὑμῶν προβλημάτων","chosen":"your speculative questions","rationale":"εἰκαῖος characterizes the proposed problems as conjectural or based on probability."},{"source_quote":"τοῖς τῶν ὅλων ἀγνοοῦσι θεόν","chosen":"since you are ignorant of the God of the universe","rationale":"The participle characterizes the hearers, while τῶν ὅλων identifies God in relation to the totality of things."}],"source_issues":[]},{"reference":"1.11","text":"As he was saying these things, they let loose disorderly laughter as though by agreement, trying to silence him and leave him at a loss, as if he were some demon-possessed barbarian. When I saw this, I was seized—I do not know how—by zeal, with pious indignation, and could no longer endure remaining silent. Instead, I cried out boldly: “God had good reason to make his will incomprehensible to you, since he foresaw that you were unworthy, as is evident from the things by which he now gives assurance to those who possess a discerning mind. For now heralds of his will have been sent out, not professing grammatical skill but disclosing his will in simple and guileless words, so that absolutely anyone who hears can understand what is said, and not with some grudging polish unwilling to make itself available to everyone. Yet you are here not only failing to understand what benefits you, but also, to your own harm, laughing at the truth that made its home among barbarians to your condemnation. Although it has now visited you as well, you do not wish to receive it as a guest, because of your licentiousness and the plainness of its words, lest you be exposed as lovers of words to no purpose and not philosophers who love truth. How long, then, will you go on learning to talk, when you do not know how to speak well? For many words from you are not worth a single reasoned statement. What, then, will your Greek multitude say, having become one soul, if there really is to be a judgment, as this man says? ‘Why, O God, did you not proclaim your will to us?’ Will you not most certainly hear—if indeed you are deemed worthy of an answer—the following? ‘Knowing before the foundation of the world every choice that would be made, I secretly met each person in advance according to what that person deserved. Wishing to assure those who have taken refuge with me of this very fact—that this is so, and why I did not from the beginning, in earlier generations, allow my will to be proclaimed publicly—I have now, near the end of life, sent heralds of my purpose. They are both laughed at and, while being abused, mocked by those who are unwilling to receive any benefit and who have vehemently rejected my friendship. Oh, what great injustice! The heralds are in danger even of being murdered, and that at the hands of the very people being called to salvation.’”","lexical_decisions":[{"source_quote":"ὡς βάρβαρόν τινα δαιμονῶντα","chosen":"as if he were some demon-possessed barbarian","rationale":"δαιμονάω can describe possession by a demon or the madness attributed to such possession; the rendering retains the explicit demonic characterization."},{"source_quote":"ἀναξίους προιδὼν ὡς ἐξ ὧν νῦν τοὺς κριτικὸν νοῦν ἔχοντας πληροφορῶν φαίνεται","chosen":"since he foresaw that you were unworthy, as is evident from the things by which he now gives assurance to those who possess a discerning mind","rationale":"The compressed syntax is taken with God as the understood subject of πληροφορῶν and ἐξ ὧν indicating the evidence from which his judgment appears."},{"source_quote":"ὡς πάνθ’ ὁντιναοῦν ἀκούσαντα νοεῖν τὰ λεγόμενα","chosen":"so that absolutely anyone who hears can understand what is said","rationale":"πάνθ’ intensifies the unrestricted ὁντιναοῦν, emphasizing accessibility to anyone whatsoever."},{"source_quote":"μετὰ ξέσεώς τινος φθονερᾶς","chosen":"with some grudging polish","rationale":"ξέσις can describe literary polishing or refinement, here portrayed as grudging because it refuses to make itself accessible to everyone."},{"source_quote":"ἐν βαρβάροις πολιτευσαμένην ἀλήθειαν","chosen":"the truth that made its home among barbarians","rationale":"πολιτεύομαι personifies truth as living or conducting its life among a people."},{"source_quote":"εἰκῇ φιλόλογοί ἐστε καὶ οὐ φιλαληθεῖς φιλόσοφοι","chosen":"lovers of words to no purpose and not philosophers who love truth","rationale":"Preserves the contrast and wordplay between devotion to words and devotion to truth."},{"source_quote":"πολλὰ γὰρ παρ’ ὑμῶν ῥήματα ἑνὸς οὐκ ἄξια λόγου","chosen":"For many words from you are not worth a single reasoned statement","rationale":"Distinguishes the many individual utterances from one meaningful or reasoned λόγος while retaining the rhetorical contrast."},{"source_quote":"ἑκάστῳ πρὸς τὸ αὐτοῦ ἄξιον λανθανόντως προαπήντησα","chosen":"I secretly met each person in advance according to what that person deserved","rationale":"The rendering retains the metaphor of meeting beforehand; πρὸς τὸ αὐτοῦ ἄξιον relates that prior encounter to each person’s deserts."},{"source_quote":"πρὸς τῷ τέλει τοῦ βίου","chosen":"near the end of life","rationale":"Preserves the edition’s βίου as “life” without replacing it with the more familiar but unsupplied “world” or “age”; whose life or course is meant remains contextually open."}],"source_issues":[]},{"reference":"1.12","text":"“‘This injustice being done against my heralds would have been done against everyone from the beginning, if the unworthy had been called to salvation from the beginning. For what is now being done unjustly by them serves as a defense of my just providence: I rightly did not wish from the beginning to expose publicly and fruitlessly to abuse the message worthy of honor. Rather, because it was precious, I resolved that it should be kept silent—not from those who were worthy from the beginning, with whom I did share it, but from these and others like them, who, as you see, are unworthy, who hate me and are unwilling to love themselves.’ Now at least, stop laughing at this man and question me about what he proclaims; or let anyone who wishes answer me when I question him. Do not bark like wanton dogs, shutting the ears of those who wish to be saved with disorderly noise. You unjust haters of God, who divert the reasoning that saves into unbelief—how can you obtain forgiveness when you insult the man who professes to tell you about the divine nature of God? And you do this to a man whom, even if he spoke nothing true, you ought to have welcomed because of his good intention toward you.”","lexical_decisions":[{"source_quote":"εἰς πάντας","chosen":"against everyone","rationale":"The masculine plural has no explicit local antecedent; it may refer to all heralds or more broadly to everyone affected, so the translation leaves the reference general."},{"source_quote":"εἰς ἀπολογίαν τῆς ἐμῆς δικαίας γίνεται προνοίας","chosen":"serves as a defense of my just providence","rationale":"ἀπολογία denotes a defense or vindication; the heralds’ present mistreatment is said to vindicate the earlier withholding."},{"source_quote":"τὸν τιμῆς ἄξιον λόγον","chosen":"the message worthy of honor","rationale":"λόγος here denotes the content being proclaimed; “message” avoids importing a personified or canonical sense."},{"source_quote":"σιγᾶσθαι αὐτὸν ὡς τίμιον","chosen":"because it was precious, I resolved that it should be kept silent","rationale":"The passive infinitive depicts the message as withheld, while τίμιος gives the reason: its precious or honored status."},{"source_quote":"καὶ νῦν γε παρέντες· γελᾶν τὸν ἄνδρα τοῦτον","chosen":"Now at least, stop laughing at this man","rationale":"Despite the printed punctuation after παρέντες, the participle is understood with γελᾶν in the established sense of leaving off or ceasing an action."},{"source_quote":"μύοντες τῶν σώζεσθαι θελόντων τὰς ἀκοάς","chosen":"shutting the ears of those who wish to be saved","rationale":"Preserves the physical image of closing the hearers’ ears rather than generalizing it as interference."},{"source_quote":"θεοστυγεῖς","chosen":"haters of God","rationale":"The compound can also be understood as “hated by God.” The active sense is chosen because the immediately preceding divine speech describes these people as hating God."},{"source_quote":"τὸν σώζοντα λογισμὸν εἰς ἀπιστίαν ἀπασχολοῦντες","chosen":"who divert the reasoning that saves into unbelief","rationale":"ἀπασχολέω conveys occupying or drawing something aside; the rendering preserves both the reasoning’s saving function and its diversion toward unbelief."},{"source_quote":"τὴν θειότητα τοῦ θεοῦ","chosen":"the divine nature of God","rationale":"θειότης denotes divinity or divine nature; the rendering retains the source’s explicit reference to God without expanding it into a later doctrinal formula."}],"source_issues":[]}]}
